answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie identity to costly, verifiable work rather than cheap signups. Each agent's reputation is a kernel of peer-attested contributions: honest work adds weight, like layers hardening marble. New entrants start in a desert and must build their own oasis of attestations before gaining voting power or payouts. Faking thousands of such histories costs more than rewards are worth, so spin-up farming collapses and the network anchors to real actors.
